name: Polyols
what_is: Polyols, also called sugar alcohols, are carbohydrates used mainly for sweetness and bulk. Common examples include sorbitol, xylitol, maltitol, erythritol, mannitol, isomalt and lactitol.
why_botia: A nutrition label may declare polyols as a single value, while the ingredient list shows which individual polyols are present. BOTIA connects those two pieces of information without assuming how much of each polyol the product contains.
can_1: Read the polyol value when it is declared on the nutrition label and preserve its unit and basis.
can_2: Identify individual polyols when they are named in the ingredient list.
can_3: Connect the declared value with the applicable regulatory information and documented evidence where relevant.
cannot_1: Determine how much of each individual polyol is present when the label gives only a combined value.
cannot_2: Predict an individual's tolerance to a polyol from the nutrition label.
cannot_3: Treat an undeclared polyol value as zero.
